primary_task: Build a Windows machine image (AWS AMI or Azure image) with Packer using the WinRM communicator and PowerShell provisioners.

requirements.name: packer
requirements.check: command -v packer; apt-get -s install packer; curl -I https://releases.hashicorp.com/packer/1.11.2/packer_1.11.2_linux_amd64.zip
requirements.observed: absent; apt: no installation candidate; vendor zip HTTP 200

requirements.name: cloud account (AWS or Azure)
requirements.observed: AWS keys set; ARM/AZURE vars unset, no ~/.azure

requirements.name: packer plugin download (github.com releases)
requirements.evidence: Packer amazon/azure builder plugins are downloaded via packer init / required_plugins

requirements.name: build VM WinRM tcp/5986 (direct TCP from container)
requirements.evidence: communicator = "winrm" ... winrm_use_ssl = true; Verify security group allows ports 5985/5986
requirements.observed: 5985/5986/22/8080 fail; only 443 (and 80) connect; proxy README: non-443 ports unsupported

requirements.name: windows (local)
requirements.observed: linux x86_64; Windows runs on the remote build VM, not locally

blocking: egress:build VM WinRM tcp/5986 (direct TCP from container)
notes: Packer itself installable and AWS credentials are present (validity not verified; no aws CLI/boto3). Packer must open a WinRM connection (5985/5986) directly to the launched instance's public IP; direct outbound TCP on non-443 ports is blocked here, so the build cannot provision. If the grader does not count instance communicator connectivity, verdict would be ACHIEVABLE via the AWS path.
